Below I give a line‑by‑line, best‑effort translation with brief glosses and notes on uncertainties. Many signs are damaged, some compound signs (and the ritual/genre of the text) leave several readings uncertain; where I am uncertain I show the Sumerian element in brackets and give a tentative rendering.

Key glosses used: ud = day; mu = day / name / year; an ki = heaven and earth; diĝir = god(s); dama‑Dinana = “the man/servant of Inanna” (dama + Dinana/Inanna); ba‑… = passive/operative verbal forms “he/it will …” or “let … be …”; dim2 ≈ “judge/decide”; tar/ta‑rar ≈ “cut off/erase”; nun = lord / exalted; kur = mountain / foreign land; keše2 = deem/assign / allocate; reduplication (‑‑‑‑) indicates intensive or plural.

1. ud re‑a‑ta ud an ki‑bi‑ta ba‑an‑[dim2‑ma‑ba]
Literal gloss: “day of his appearing / day of heaven‑and‑earth — (he) will be judged.”
Translation (tentative): “On the day of his appearing, on the day of heaven and earth, he shall be judged.”

Note: re‑a‑ta = “the day of his coming/appearance”; dim2 = judge/decree (reading uncertain).

2. ĝi6 re‑a‑ta ĝi6 an ki‑bi‑ta /ba\‑[an‑dim2‑ma‑ba]
Literal gloss: “(variant) day of his appearing / day of heaven‑and‑earth — (he) will be judged.”
Translation (tentative): “On his day of coming, on the day of heaven and earth, he shall be judged.”

Note: ĝi6 here seems to parallel ud in line 1 (variant term for “day/occasion”); the final clause repeats the judgment formula.

3. [mu re]‑a‑/ta\ mu nam ba‑[tar‑ra‑ba]
Literal gloss: “day/ year of his coming — his name will be cut off.”
Translation (tentative): “On that day (or in that year) his name shall be erased.”

Note: ba‑tar = “to cut off/expunge (a name)”; this is a common curse/formulaic threat.

4. [da]‑/nun\-na‑ke4‑ne ba‑tu‑ud‑da‑a‑ba
Literal gloss: “to/for the great lord / to the exalted one — he will be handed over / delivered.”
Translation (tentative): “He shall be given over to the great/exalted lord.”

Note: reading of the divine title (da‑nun/da‑nunna) is uncertain; ba‑tuud = “be delivered/assigned.”

5. dama‑dinana nam‑NIR.PA‑še3 ba‑tuku‑a‑ba
Literal gloss: “the servant/man of Inanna — the name NIR.PA — (he) has established/caused.”
Translation (tentative): “The servant of Inanna has (thus) set up the name ‘NIR.PA’.”

Note: NIR.PA is a sign‑cluster whose precise sense here is uncertain (possibly a technical name/title).

6. dama‑dinana an ki‑a ba‑ḫal‑ḫal‑la‑a‑ba
Literal gloss: “the servant of Inanna — heaven and earth — (he) made tremble/intensely moved.”
Translation (tentative): “The servant of Inanna made heaven and earth tremble.”

Note: ḫal‑ḫal (reduplication) = intensified action (make tremble/quake/shake).

7. dama‑dinana […] ba‑a‑peš u3‑tud‑da‑a‑ba
Literal gloss: “the servant of Inanna … (he) caused to go forth / performed — day/birth(?) he gave.”
Translation (tentative): “The servant of Inanna … performed (the act) and gave a day/title.”

Note: lacuna (…); u3‑tud could be “day-name” or “birth/begotten” depending on context.

8. diĝir kurum6‑ma‑bi A X X unu2?‑bi‑še3 ba‑ab‑keše2‑a‑<ba>
Literal gloss: “the gods of the mountain(s) / the mountain‑gods — A X X — he assigned/allocated.”
Translation (tentative): “The mountain‑gods … he assigned (them) [rest of the line lost].”

Note: several signs broken (X); ba‑ab‑keše2 = “he set aside / he allocated / he accounted.”

9. diĝir šar2‑šar2 kiĝ2‑ĝa2 al‑sug2‑ge‑eš diĝir tur‑tur du2‑lum im‑il2‑il2‑e‑ne
Literal gloss: “gods king‑king / holy‑office — not settle? — gods many‑many / binding/wrapping — (he) caused to go forth repeatedly.”
Translation (tentative): “The gods of kingship and holy office would not be established; the many gods bound/arrayed, he led them forth.”

Note: this is highly schematic; many compounds here are ritual/technical and the line appears to describe divine mobilization or disorder.

10. diĝir id2 <im> dun‑dun‑u3‑ne saḫar‑bi ḫa‑ra‑li im‑dub‑dub‑be2‑ne
Literal gloss: “gods of the river/stream (?) — (sound?) — renew‑renew — their SAḪAR(?) — (?) — he wrote (?)/he inscribed (?);”
Translation (tentative): “The gods of the (river/region) … renewed; the saḫar (a term/name) he inscribed/wrote upon them.”

Note: id2, saḫar, ḫarali and the verbal sequence are uncertain; im‑dub‑dub may indicate repeated inscriptive action.

11. diĝir im ar3‑ar3‑re‑ne zi‑bi inim am3‑ma‑ĝar‑re‑ne
Literal gloss: “gods of wind(?) / storms (?) — life(?) — word/speech — ‘not to come’ (?)”
Translation (tentative): “The gods of wind (or storm) — life and speech — (he) caused the word ‘do not come’ to be declared.”

Note: ar3‑ar3 and am3‑ma reflect reduplication; inim = “word/command”; exact sense uncertain.

12. ud‑ba ĝeštug2 daĝal mud diĝir šar2‑šar2 ĝal2‑ĝal2
Literal gloss: “day‑?? hand/arm great? … gods of kingship multiplied/intensified”
Translation (tentative): “On that day the great arm (power) of the gods of kingship was greatly increased.”

Note: ĝeštug2 = “wrist/hand/arm / power”; mud = possibly “to be elevated”; ĝal2‑ĝal2 intensifies.

13. den‑ki‑ke4 engur buru3 a‑sur‑ra ki diĝir na‑me šag4‑bi u6 nu‑um‑me
Literal gloss: “to Lord‑of‑the‑earth (Enki?) the subterranean / the mountain‑border — the land, the gods’ names / their good? day not exist?”
Translation (tentative): “To the Lord of the Land (Enki) of the deep/foundation and the border‑lands — the names of the gods and their good days shall not be.”

Note: complicated; engur = Abzu/primeval water; nu‑um‑me = “not be/cease”.

14. ki‑nu2‑ni i3‑nu2 u3 ku nu‑um‑zi‑zi
Literal gloss: “this place/land — here — day and night — not to rest/never cease (?)”
Translation (tentative): “In this land, here, day and night shall not rest/shall not be calm.”

Note: nu‑um‑zi‑zi (reduplication) = continuing negation / “never.”

15. diĝir er2‑ra im‑pad‑pad‑ne a‑nir ĝal2 i3‑ak im‑me‑ne
Literal gloss: “gods of earth(?) — he caused to press down — mighty … he placed/let stand.”
Translation (tentative): “The earth‑gods he pressed down and made mighty; he set them in place.”

Note: er2‑ra often soil/earth; pad‑pad = pressing; a‑nir uncertain.

16. lu2 ku‑ra i3‑nu2‑a‑ra ki‑nu2‑bi nu‑um‑zi‑zi‑<ra>
Literal gloss: “man (person) of Kura/Kur — here/this day/this place — his land shall not rest.”
Translation (tentative): “The man of Kura — in this place — his land shall not have rest.”

Note: ku‑ra = Kur/Kura (region/place); lu2 ku‑ra could be a title or ethnic designation.

17. dnamma‑ke4 ama palil u3‑tud diĝir šar2‑šar2‑ra‑ke4‑ne
Literal gloss: “to his mother Namma? the many births / day‑name — the gods of kingship/their … ”
Translation (tentative): “To his mother Namma(?) — repeated birth/day‑names — to the gods of kingship (they belong).”

Note: namma is a divine/maternal title; palil = “many times”; u3‑tud = day/birth.

18. er2‑ra diĝir‑re‑e‑ne dumu‑ni‑ir ba‑ši‑in‑de6
Literal gloss: “earth(?) — his gods — his son? dumu‑ni‑ir — he made to sit/appoint.”
Translation (tentative): “Earth and his gods — his son Niar(?) he set/appointed.”

Note: dumu‑ni‑ir reads as name or title; ba‑šin‑de6 = “he placed/appointed.”

19. X mu‑un‑ši‑nu2‑u3‑nam u3 mu‑un‑ši‑ku‑ku‑na‑nam
Literal gloss: “X — ‘you shall not be pronounced/name’ and ‘you shall not be known’.”
Translation (tentative): “(May) X not be named; may X not be known.”

Note: mu‑un‑ši‑… = negative commands about naming; duplicate formula (mu‑un‑ši‑ku‑ku) intensifies.

20. [X] TE BA [… nu‑mu‑un]‑zi‑zi
Literal gloss: “[X] — TE (tablet/command) be — … you shall not continue.”
Translation (tentative): “[X] — let the tablet/command be — … that you shall not persist.”

Note: TE sign could mean “to cut/erase” or “tablet”; nu‑mu‑un‑zi‑zi = “you shall not continue/there shall be no more.”

21. dim3‑me2‑er šu dim2‑dim2‑ma‑zu X gu2?‑bi im‑tu10‑tu10‑ne
Literal gloss: “judge‑man/extent? hand — judge/judge‑again — X house? (gu2) he caused to go/execute repeatedly.”
Translation (tentative): “The judge enacted this by his hand; (the) house/thing X he repeatedly executed.”

Note: dim3, dim2 are related to judgment/ordaining; im‑tu10‑tu10 (reduplication) = repeated action.

Overall interpretative summary (tentative)
- The text looks like a ritual/curse or an oracle: a sequence of days/occasions and formulae invoking heaven and earth, gods, and the servant/man of Inanna. Common motifs are judgment, erasure of a name, delivery over to a lord/judge, the unsettling or trembling of heaven and earth, assignment or inscription by the gods, and explicit prohibitions that a person/name not be spoken or persist. Many lines are lacunose or use rare compound signs; consequently the above translation is provisional and preserves the broad sense rather than a strictly philological edition.

- attempt a more literal morpheme‑by‑morpheme gloss line by line,
- mark every uncertain sign and give alternative readings,
- or try to situate the text with parallels (e.g. curse formulae erasing names, or Inanna‑related liturgies) — tell me which you prefer.
